assumptions: Kinematic motion with static solid obstacles and conservative swept body envelopes; no automatic path planner.
Uniform device scale changes the rendered body, clearance, mounting offsets and takeoff/landing heights.
Configured speed and sensor ranges are assumptions, not measurements from a hardware vendor.
No battery, acceleration, radio, moving-device collision, dynamic cargo collision or hardware calibration.
Workflows execute typed commands in sequence; they are scripts, not an embedded autonomous model.
Only kinematic travel and configured per-step dwell consume simulated time. Inspection and arm preset commands have no calibrated hardware duration.
Coverage counts sampled floor checkpoints, not full areas or exhaustive inventory.
Drafts and the last 32 runs live in memory. Export JSON to keep them across restarts.

conclusion: Under static kinematic assumptions the configured 3 m/s rover completes the identical 107.708 m, three-cargo inspection loop 23.935 simulated seconds sooner (36.4% shorter duration), with equal completion and checkpoint metrics. This is a sensitivity result for configured speed, not evidence of real hardware speed, safety, battery, sensing reliability, or calibration. Recommend hardware validation before procurement.
transportRecovery: Initial tools:true fetch failed with EPERM on loopback. Retried with explicitly enabled network permissions; succeeded. No MCP command or trial errors.
